title: runtime/kv: fix rare race between compaction moves and decode stream sync; add stress test
author: Grace Kim
release_notes: Fixes a rare correctness issue in KV compaction under concurrent decode; adds a stress test to prevent regressions. No API/behavior changes; compaction remains behind the runtime flag.
description: Context: With KV compaction enabled, we move KV blocks to reduce fragmentation. Under a specific interleaving of (a) decode kernels enqueued on the per-model decode stream and (b) a compaction move that updates block metadata/pointers, we can observe a rare race where the move is committed before the decode stream has fully observed the required sync point. This shows up as occasional invalid reads (silent quality blips) or, more often, a device-side fault when long-context traffic forces frequent moves. This was first suspected during PM-2025-02-11 follow-up debugging and reproduced in the ENG-2849 stress harness when forcing aggressive compaction triggers. Root cause: we relied on a stream-wide sync primitive that guarded allocator bookkeeping but did not correctly gate per-sequence “in-flight” decode work when decode work was queued after the last observed event; additionally, the compaction commit path could publish the new physical location to the block table before we had a hard dependency on the decode stream completing reads of the old location. Fix: introduce an explicit per-sequence decode fence (CUDA event) that is recorded on the decode stream at the point the sequence last enqueues attention reads for the current token, and require compaction moves for that sequence to wait on that event prior to (1) memcpy/move and (2) publishing pointer remap in the block table. The compaction engine now uses a two-phase commit: phase A performs the copy after waiting on the decode fence; phase B atomically swaps the mapping and marks the old blocks reclaimable only after a second event confirms the copy stream has completed. This avoids a global device sync and keeps the fast path cheap. Added a regression test that runs concurrent prefill/decode with forced compaction every N tokens and random stream scheduling jitter; it failed ~1/2k runs before the fix on A100 and H100 when run with high concurrency. Notes: no changes to scheduler policy in this PR; this is purely correctness/sync. Compaction flag remains default-off. References: PM-2025-02-11 (incident follow-up), Slack thread 1739728004 (minimal reproducer), and prior compaction work in PRs #18457/#18463.
commits: runtime/kv: add per-sequence decode fence primitive (cuda event wrapper)
runtime/kv: gate compaction move/cutover on decode fence; two-phase publish
runtime/kv: tighten block-table publish ordering (acquire/release) + comments
tests/runtime: add kv_compaction_decode_race_stress test (forced moves + jitter)
docs/dev: note new invariants in compaction engine (stream + publish ordering)
conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Thanks for chasing this down. Can you clarify why we need the second event (copy-complete) if we already wait on decode before copying? Concern is reclaim of old blocks while copy stream is still in-flight.

Grace Kim (author): Yep—decode-fence ensures readers are done with *old* location, but without copy-complete we could reclaim/compact further while the copy stream is still writing *new* location. The second event gates "publish old blocks free" and avoids another move choosing the newly-targeted blocks prematurely. Added comment in commit 3.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Any perf impact? Specifically: are we recording an event every token for every active seq? That could be expensive at high TPS.

Grace Kim (author): We record the fence only when compaction is enabled AND the sequence is eligible for move (movable segments enabled). Additionally, we reuse an event from a small pool per worker; recording is ~2–3us on our bench and is amortized by move frequency (we don’t move every token). I added a microbenchmark note in docs and a TODO to consider event-less counters if needed.

Yuki Sato (review): The publish ordering in block_table: I see the release store on new mapping. Where’s the corresponding acquire load on readers? Want to ensure kernels don’t read partially-updated metadata.

Grace Kim (author): Readers already go through block_table::lookup() which now uses an acquire load (added in this PR). Also, the mapping update is single pointer-sized value; metadata update happens before publish. I added a brief comment on the invariants in docs/dev/runtime/kv_compaction_invariants.md.
Rafael Mendes (review / SRE): Please add an incident reference in the PR body + mention what log line/metric we can use if this regresses during canary.

Grace Kim (author): Added incident follow-up ref (PM-2025-02-11) and a note: if this regresses, you typically see `kv.compaction.move_wait_decode_ms` spikes + occasional `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` tagged with `kv_compaction_move`. (Metric name already landed in #18423.)
Grace Kim (author): Increased max iterations but added early-exit on failure; also reduced per-iteration sleep jitter upper bound. Re-ran CI.
